name: Preserve on Compaction
description: During context compaction, preserve critical information like file lists, test commands, and current task state.
content:
# Preserve on Compaction Rules

- Always preserve the list of files you've modified in this session — losing track means missing files in commits
- Preserve exact test commands and their expected output — you'll need to re-verify after compaction
- Preserve the current task description and acceptance criteria — don't lose sight of what you're trying to accomplish
- Preserve any error messages or stack traces you're actively debugging — re-reading files to find them again wastes time
- Preserve the branch name and git state (staged/unstaged changes) — this context is critical for commits
- Preserve environment-specific details — ports, URLs, database names, config file locations
- Preserve decisions already made and their reasoning — don't re-debate settled questions
- Preserve the user's preferences and constraints they've stated — these are non-negotiable requirements
- If you reference a handoff document, re-read it after compaction to refresh your context
- Keep a mental model of the project structure — which directories matter, what the architecture looks like
- Preserve any pending TODOs or follow-up tasks the user has requested
- When context is getting long, proactively summarize progress before compaction forces it on you
